name: SiteGPT
tagline: A bootstrapped, code-executing AI chatbot that went from weekend project to real recurring revenue without a dollar of outside funding.
tldr: SiteGPT is a no-code AI chatbot builder trained on your website and documents, distinguished by letting the bot run code snippets and connect directly to a database mid-conversation, not just answer from static text.

Pricing runs Starter ($39/mo, 4,000 messages, 1,000 pages), Growth ($79/mo, 10,000 messages, 10,000 pages), Scale ($259/mo, 40,000 messages, 50,000 pages, Zendesk integration), and custom Enterprise (up to 500,000 pages, HIPAA eligibility).

Founded in 2023 by solo/bootstrapped founder Bhanu Teja P (also credited as Bhanu Teja Pasala/Pachipulusu), based in India, with no external funding — reportedly reached around $300K ARR by mid-2024 from a standing start.

Reviews show a familiar split-review pattern: Product Hunt and G2/Capterra scores land around 4.1-4.5/5 with praise for the code-execution and database-connection features, while Trustpilot-style aggregators run noticeably lower, and some reviewers report billing/account-access issues after payment.
No free trial is offered, which several reviewers specifically call out as a trust barrier before committing to a paid plan.
keyFeatures: Ability to run executable code snippets and connect directly to a database from within a conversation, going beyond static content retrieval
Trains on up to 500,000 pages at the Enterprise tier, scaling from 1,000 pages on the entry Starter plan
Auto-refresh scheduling (manual on lower tiers, weekly on Scale, daily on Enterprise) to keep trained content current
Native Zendesk integration and webhook support on the Scale tier for connecting into an existing support stack
AI conversation insights and advanced analytics for reviewing what customers are actually asking
iOS app for managing chatbots and conversations on the go
API access from the Growth tier upward for embedding chatbot logic into custom applications
HIPAA eligibility and signed agreements available at the Enterprise tier for compliance-sensitive buyers

faq.question: What makes SiteGPT different from a basic website chatbot?
faq.answer: Its standout feature is the ability to execute code snippets and connect to a database mid-conversation, which reviewers specifically call out as differentiating it from chatbots that can only retrieve static trained text.

faq.question: How is SiteGPT priced?
faq.answer: Message- and page-volume tiered plans: Starter $39/mo (4,000 messages, 1,000 pages), Growth $79/mo (10,000 messages, 10,000 pages), Scale $259/mo (40,000 messages, 50,000 pages, Zendesk integration), and custom Enterprise up to 500,000 pages. Add-ons include branding removal (+$39/mo) and extra message blocks (+$39/mo per 5,000).

faq.question: Is there a free trial?
faq.answer: No — SiteGPT does not offer a free trial, which multiple reviewers flag as a barrier to trusting the product before paying, especially compared to competitors like Chatbase that offer a free tier.

faq.question: Who built SiteGPT?
faq.answer: It was built by a bootstrapped, largely solo founder (credited as Bhanu Teja P) starting in 2023, growing to a reported ~$300K ARR by mid-2024 without external venture funding.

faq.question: Does SiteGPT integrate with existing helpdesk tools?
faq.answer: Yes, a native Zendesk integration and webhook support are available starting on the Scale tier ($259/mo), letting it plug into an existing support workflow rather than replace it outright.

scorecard.note: Reviewers describe it as super easy to train and integrate, with quick website-content ingestion.
The code-execution and live database connection capability is repeatedly singled out as more accurate and capable than static-retrieval competitors.
Effectively a website-widget-and-API product — no native WhatsApp, social DM, or voice channel documented.
Competitive per-message pricing at entry, but no free trial and add-on costs (branding removal, extra messages) add up quickly at scale.
Some reviewers report broken billing/account-access flows and weak support handoff after payment, a real concern for a bootstrapped, presumably small team.

pricing.model: Tiered SaaS by monthly message volume and trained page count

pros: Genuinely differentiated technical capability — running code and connecting to a live database mid-conversation, not just retrieving static text
Scales to very large trained content sets (up to 500,000 pages on Enterprise), suited to large documentation-heavy sites
Native Zendesk integration and webhooks make it easier to slot into an existing support stack rather than replace it
Bootstrapped, profitable-trending company history suggests a founder incentivized to keep the product working, not chase a growth-at-all-costs exit
cons: No free trial, which multiple reviewers specifically cite as a reason they hesitated to buy
No native messaging channels beyond the website widget and API — no WhatsApp, social DM, or voice
Some reviewers report billing and account-access problems after paying, plus weaker support handoff than larger competitors
Add-on costs (branding removal, extra message blocks) stack onto already-tiered pricing, complicating total cost

sentiment.quote: SiteGPT is much better in terms of features...the only chatbot that allows automating customer facing tasks by letting me run code snippets and connect to my database
It's super easy to train and integrate. Moreover, I was able to add executionary functions
I paid for the essential plan but don't have access to creating any chatbot

bestFor: Technical teams that want a chatbot capable of executing code or querying a live database, not just answering FAQs
Large content sites needing to train on tens or hundreds of thousands of pages
Businesses already using Zendesk that want an AI layer bolted onto that existing workflow
Buyers comfortable committing without a free trial, based on documented feature depth
verdict: SiteGPT's code-execution and database-connection capability is a real, specific technical edge over most website-widget chatbots on this list — it's the difference between a bot that can look something up live versus one that just paraphrases a crawled page. But the lack of a free trial is a genuine friction point competitors like Chatbase don't have, and the Product Hunt reports of paying customers losing access to their chatbot are the kind of specific, concrete complaint worth weighing seriously against a company this size. Worth a serious look if the code-execution feature is actually load-bearing for your use case; skip it if you just need a straightforward FAQ bot, where cheaper, better-trialed options exist.
